Description: The quadric surfaces, which the first solid.offset case never reached: a ball of radius 20, a torus with major radius 30 and minor radius 8, and a truncated cone from radius 20 at z=0 to radius 8 at z=30. Each is grown and shrunk, and each result is known in closed form, because the offset of a quadric is the same quadric with a changed radius. The fourth body combines all three with a plane: the cone, a torus laid around its base circle and a ball set on its top, so the offset has to deal with the intersection curves between cone, sphere and torus, not just with the isolated surfaces.
Expected: BALL: +5 is a ball of radius 25, V = 4/3*pi*25^3 = 65449.8469, A = 4*pi*625 = 7853.9816; -5 is radius 15, V = 14137.1669, A = 2827.4334. TORUS: only the minor radius changes, so +3 gives 30/11 with V = 2*pi^2*30*121 = 71653.3280 and A = 4*pi^2*30*11 = 13027.8778, and -3 gives 30/5 with V = 14804.4066 and A = 5921.7626. CONE: with tan(beta) = 12/30, shrinking by 4 gives the same half angle with radii 20-4/cos(beta)-4*tan(beta) = 14.0919 and 8+4*tan(beta)-4/cos(beta) = 5.2919 over a height of 22, so V = pi*22/3*(R1^2+R1*R2+R2^2) = 6938.1575 and A = pi*(R1+R2)*s+pi*R1^2+pi*R2^2 with s = 23.6947 = 2154.7459. Growing by 4 is the Steiner formula of the convex cone: V0 = 19603.5382, A0 = 4299.9220, mean curvature integral M = pi*h + pi*R1*(pi/2+beta) + pi*R2*(pi/2-beta) = 246.7670, so V = V0+A0*4+M*16+4*pi/3*64 = 41019.5807 and A = A0+2*M*4+4*pi*16 = 6475.1199. The grown cone must show a toroidal face at each of the two circular edges and no sphere, since no vertex exists. COMBINED: no closed form; the invariants are that both offsets come out as one closed, consistent solid and that the surface histogram still carries all four kinds - ConicalSurface, SphericalSurface, ToroidalSurface and PlaneSurface - with the rounded convex edges adding further toroidal faces.
Status: KNOWN FAIL (2026-09-10). The cone half of this case is fixed - see Actual - what is left is the combined body, which fails in both directions. No baseline yet; once the combined offsets work, judge the result, regenerate and set CaseStatus to Ok. Note the runtime: one run takes about two minutes, which is why Repeat is 2 and not 4 here.
Actual:
SECOND MEASUREMENT (2026-09-10, after the cone offset fix in ConicalSurface.GetOffsetSurface and ShellExtensions.GetOffset; two repeats, identical). Both cone offsets are correct now and hit their closed forms: coneGrown 41019.5806941 / 6475.1198956 against the Steiner values 41019.5807 / 6475.1199 (1e-9), on ConicalSurface:1 PlaneSurface:2 ToroidalSurface:2 - a toroidal fillet at each of the two circular edges and no sphere, exactly as Expected demands; coneShrunk 6938.15747558 / 2154.7458959 against 6938.1575 / 2154.7459 (1e-8), on ConicalSurface:1 PlaneSurface:2. Ball and torus are unchanged (torus exact to 1e-9, ball within 6e-5 of the closed form, the mesh bias of a spherical face). Still open is the combined body: combinedGrown +3 now comes back EMPTY rather than throwing - reported as E_OPERATION_FAILED, since growing must never be empty - and combinedShrunk -3 still fails with 'lenth of knots and poles not compatible with degree', the same NURBS error as in OffsetClosesPinholeCavity. The remaining defect is therefore in the patchwork of the intersecting quadrics, not in the offset of a single quadric.
FIRST MEASUREMENT (2026-09-09, before the fix), for the record: three of the six offsets failed. coneGrown +4 threw a NullReferenceException; coneShrunk -4 SUCCEEDED but stored nothing, taking the empty-result path although the answer was a well defined truncated cone; combinedGrown gave 'Error in the application' and combinedShrunk the NURBS error. Cause of the two cone failures: for a cone whose used v range is negative - which is what solid.cone builds, apex above the body - GetOffsetSurface returned the offset for -offset, and the cone branch in ShellExtensions dereferenced the projected curve before its null check.
